Noah: Hebrew, from Noach, usually explained as 'rest' or 'comfort'. The biblical ark builder; Noa is the girls' form.
Olivia: Latin, from oliva 'olive'; the olive tree symbolises peace. Popularised by Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.
Arthur: Celtic origin of uncertain meaning, possibly 'bear' (Welsh arth) or a Roman clan name Artorius. Famous from the legendary King Arthur.
Liam: Irish short form of Uilliam, the Irish form of William, from Germanic 'will' and 'helmet', meaning resolute protector.
Jules: French form of Julius, a Latin clan name of uncertain meaning, possibly 'youthful' or 'downy-bearded'.
Louis: French form of Ludwig, from Germanic hlod 'famed' and wig 'battle', meaning famous warrior. Borne by many French kings.
Adam: Hebrew, 'man' or 'earth', related to adamah 'ground'. The first man in the Bible; also common in Arabic as Adam.
Emma: Germanic, from ermen 'whole' or 'universal'. Introduced to England by Emma of Normandy.
Gabriel: Hebrew, 'God is my strength' (or 'strong man of God'). The archangel who announces Jesus's birth; Gabrielle is the feminine.
Louise: French feminine of Louis, from Germanic 'famed warrior'.
Lucas: Latin Lucas, from Greek Loukas, 'man from Lucania' or related to Latin lux 'light'. Form of Luke.
Lina: Short form of names ending in -lina such as Caroline or Adelina; in Arabic it also means 'tender' or 'palm tree'.
Sofia: Greek sophia, 'wisdom'. Common across Europe; variant of Sophia.
Alice: Old French form of Adelais, from Germanic adal 'noble' and heid 'kind', meaning noble. Popularised by Alice in Wonderland.
Victor: Latin, 'conqueror' or 'victor', from vincere 'to conquer'. Borne by several early popes and saints.
Juliette: French diminutive of Julie, itself from Latin Julia, a Roman clan name. Famous from Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet.
Mila: Slavic short form of names with mil 'dear, gracious', such as Ludmila. Also used as an independent modern name.
Anna: Hebrew Channah, 'grace' or 'favour'. Mother of the Virgin Mary in tradition; widespread across Europe.
Eva: Latin and Greek form of Eve, from Hebrew Chavvah, 'life' or 'living'.
Oscar: Irish Gaelic, probably 'deer lover' or 'friend of deer'. Popularised by Ossian poems; also linked to Old English 'divine spear'.
Leon: Greek leon 'lion', via Latin Leo. Used in Dutch, German, Polish and other languages.
Nora: Short form of Eleonora or Honora, from Latin honor 'honour'; also used independently in Irish and Scandinavian contexts.
Mia: Italian and Scandinavian 'mine', also a short form of Maria. Used internationally.
Lucie: French form of Lucia, from Latin lux 'light', meaning light-born.
Matteo: Italian form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Mohamed: Arabic, 'praised' or 'praiseworthy', from the root h-m-d. Name of the Prophet of Islam; a spelling variant of Muhammad.
Ella: Germanic short form of names with ali 'other' or adal 'noble', or from Eleanor; also an independent name meaning 'beautiful fairy' in some traditions.
Léon: French form of Leon, from Greek leon 'lion'.
Jade: English and French, from the gemstone, via Spanish piedra de ijada 'stone of the flank'. A modern virtue-like name.
Luca: Italian form of Luke, from Greek Loukas, 'man from Lucania' or 'light'.
Inaya: Arabic, 'care', 'concern' or 'protection'; also spelled Inaya or Inayah.
Elena: Spanish, Italian and Russian form of Helen, from Greek, probably 'torch' or 'bright one'.
Alba: Latin albus 'white', also 'dawn' in Spanish, Italian and Catalan. Used in Romance-speaking countries.
Julia: Latin feminine of Julius, a Roman clan name of uncertain meaning, possibly 'youthful'.
Victoria: Latin, 'victory'. Roman goddess of victory; popularised by Queen Victoria.
Luna: Latin, 'moon'. Also the Roman moon goddess; a recent popular name.
Finn: Irish Fionn 'fair' or Norse Finnr 'wanderer' or 'Sami'. Also borne by the legendary hero Fionn mac Cumhaill.
Lewis: English and Scottish form of Louis, from Germanic 'famous warrior'.
Raphaël: Hebrew, 'God has healed'. The archangel Raphael; French form of Raphael.
Noor: Arabic, 'light', from nur. Used for girls and boys in Muslim communities.
Nina: Possibly Spanish 'girl' or a short form of names such as Antonina or Anna; also Russian and Quechua origins have been proposed. Origin uncertain.
Mathis: French and German form of Matthias, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Giulia: Italian form of Julia, from the Roman clan name Julius.
Elias: Greek form of Elijah, from Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'.
Amir: Arabic, 'prince' or 'commander'; also Hebrew 'treetop' in some contexts. Used in Arabic, Persian and Hebrew.
Marie: French form of Maria, from Hebrew Miriam, whose meaning is uncertain, possibly 'beloved' or 'wished-for child'. Mother of Jesus.
Ellie: English diminutive of Eleanor or Elizabeth, now also independent. Eleanor possibly from Provençal Aliénor.
Hugo: Germanic, from hug 'heart, mind, spirit'. Made famous by writer Victor Hugo.
Théo: French short form of Théodore, from Greek 'gift of God' (theos 'god' and doron 'gift').
Rayan: Arabic, 'luxuriant' or 'watered'; Ar-Rayyan is a gate of paradise in Islam.
Léa: French form of Leah, Hebrew, possibly 'weary' or 'wild cow'. Biblical wife of Jacob.
Achille: French form of Achilles, Greek hero of the Trojan War; meaning uncertain, possibly 'pain' (achos).
Lou: French short form of Louis or Louise, also used independently; from Germanic 'famed warrior'.
Otis: English from Ode, a Germanic name meaning 'wealth' or 'fortune'; also an English surname.
Léo: French form of Leo, from Latin leo 'lion'.
Camille: French, from Latin Camillus, a Roman family name, possibly 'attendant at a religious rite'. Used for both sexes in France.
Liv: Scandinavian, 'life' or 'protection', from Old Norse hlif. Also a short form of Olivia.
Mona: Irish Muadhnait 'noble'; also Greek monos 'single' and Arabic 'wish'. Origin depends on culture.
Livia: Latin, a Roman clan name possibly from 'livid' or 'bluish', or from 'olive'. Famous as the wife of Augustus.
Lily: English, from the flower, a symbol of purity.
Renée: French, 'reborn', from Latin renatus. Masculine form is René.
Billie: English, originally a feminine or diminutive of William, 'resolute protector'.
Marcel: French from Latin Marcellus, diminutive of Marcus, probably linked to the war god Mars.
Chloé: French form of Chloe, Greek 'green shoot' or 'blooming'. An epithet of the goddess Demeter.
Eden: Hebrew, 'delight' or 'pleasure'; the garden of Eden in Genesis.
Sacha: French form of Sasha, Russian short form of Alexander, from Greek 'defender of men'.
Lena: Short form of names such as Helena or Magdalena; Greek-derived, 'torch' or 'bright'.
Jeanne: French feminine of Jean, from Hebrew Yochanan, 'God is gracious'. Associated with Joan of Arc.
Nathan: Hebrew, 'he gave' or 'God has given'. Biblical prophet in David's court.
Isaac: Hebrew, 'he laughs' or 'he will laugh'. Son of Abraham in the Bible.
Nour: Arabic, 'light'; French transcription of Nur, used for girls and boys.
Alix: French medieval form of Alice, from Germanic 'noble kind'; also used for boys as a short form of Alexis.
Theo: Short form of Theodore (Greek 'gift of God') or Theodoor; widely used in Dutch and German.
Emile: French Émile, from Latin Aemilius, a Roman clan name possibly from aemulus 'rival'.
Felix: Latin, 'happy' or 'fortunate'. Borne by several saints and popes.
Milo: Germanic, possibly 'merciful' or 'soldier'; also Slavic mil 'dear'. Origin uncertain.
Maël: Breton, from mael 'prince' or 'chief'. Common in Brittany and France.
Basile: French form of Basil, from Greek basileios 'royal' or 'kingly'.
Leo: Latin, 'lion'. Borne by thirteen popes; used across Europe.
Charles: French and English, from Germanic karl 'free man'. Borne by Charlemagne and many kings.
Emiel: Flemish form of Emile, from Latin Aemilius, a Roman clan name.
Amélie: French form of Amalia, from Germanic amal 'work' or 'industrious'.
Ibrahim: Arabic form of Abraham, from Hebrew, 'father of many'. A prophet of Islam.
Emilia: Latin feminine of Aemilius, a Roman clan name possibly from 'rival'. Also linked to Germanic amal 'work'.
Georges: French form of George, from Greek georgos 'farmer', literally 'earth worker'.
Romy: German and French, short form of Rosemarie, or from Romaine 'Roman'. Popularised by actress Romy Schneider.
Oliver: Old French Olivier, possibly from Latin oliva 'olive' or Germanic 'elf army'. Origin debated.
Henri: French form of Henry, from Germanic heim 'home' and ric 'ruler', meaning home ruler.
Naël: Modern French name, probably from Arabic Nael 'one who attains' or a form of Noël 'Christmas'. Origin uncertain.
Rose: English and French, from the flower; also associated with Germanic hros 'horse' or 'fame'.
Yanis: Greek Yannis, a form of John, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'; also used in North African communities.
Noé: French form of Noah, Hebrew 'rest' or 'comfort'.
Gaspard: French form of Caspar, one of the Magi; probably Persian, 'treasurer'.
Aya: Arabic 'sign' or 'verse of the Quran'; also Hebrew 'bird' and Japanese 'colour'. Origin varies by culture.
Maurice: French from Latin Mauritius, 'dark-skinned' or 'Moorish', from Maurus. Saint Maurice was a Roman soldier.
Elise: French short form of Elisabeth, from Hebrew 'God is my oath'.
David: Hebrew, 'beloved'. The biblical king of Israel.
Imran: Arabic, from Amram, perhaps 'prosperous' or 'long-lived'. Name of the father of Mary in the Quran.
William: Germanic, from wil 'will' and helm 'helmet', meaning resolute protector. Brought to England by the Normans.
Gaston: French, probably from Germanic 'guest' or 'stranger'; also connected to the region Gascony.
Sara: Hebrew, 'princess'. Wife of Abraham; also Arabic Sara 'joy'.
Mohammed: Arabic, 'praised' or 'praiseworthy'. Name of the Prophet of Islam; spelling variant of Muhammad.
Charlotte: French feminine diminutive of Charles, from Germanic karl 'free man'.
Lio: Probably a modern short form of Leo or Elio, from Latin 'lion' or Greek 'sun'. Origin uncertain.
Alexander: Greek, 'defender of men', from alexein and aner. Borne by Alexander the Great.
Ambre: French, 'amber', from Arabic anbar. Gemstone name.
Iris: Greek, 'rainbow'. Greek goddess messenger of the gods; also the flower.
César: French and Spanish form of Caesar, a Roman family name of uncertain meaning, possibly 'hairy' or 'blue-eyed'.
Zayn: Arabic, 'beauty' or 'grace', short for Zain or Zayn al-Din.
Ada: Germanic short form of names with adal 'noble'; also Hebrew Adah 'adornment'. Famous through Ada Lovelace.
Sophia: Greek, 'wisdom'. Used in Christian and royal traditions.
Milan: Slavic, from mil 'dear' or 'gracious'; also the Italian city, probably Celtic 'middle of the plain'.
Aaron: Hebrew, of uncertain meaning, possibly 'mountain of strength' or 'exalted'. Brother of Moses.
Charlie: English diminutive of Charles, from Germanic karl 'free man'.
Lara: Russian short form of Larisa, perhaps Greek 'cheerful'; in Latin also Lara, a nymph. Also Catalan form.
Lucien: French from Latin Lucianus, derived from Lucius, from lux 'light'.
Clara: Latin, 'bright' or 'clear'. Saint Clare of Assisi.
Ali: Arabic, 'high', 'elevated' or 'exalted'. Cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad.
Maria: Latin and Greek form of Mary, from Hebrew Miriam, whose meaning is uncertain.
Manon: French diminutive of Marie, from Hebrew Miriam. Popularised by Prévost's novel Manon Lescaut.
Viktor: Germanic spelling of Victor, from Latin 'conqueror'.
Vic: Short form of Victor, Latin 'conqueror'; also of Victoria.
Gust: Flemish short form of Gustaaf or August, from Latin 'venerable'.
Ayden: Modern spelling of Aidan, from Irish Aodhán, 'little fire'. Variant forms also used in Turkish.
Rosalie: French, from Latin rosalia, a Roman festival of roses. Also a form of Rose.
Owen: Welsh Owain, possibly from Latin Eugenius 'well-born' or from 'young warrior'. Origin debated.
Robin: Diminutive of Robert, from Germanic hrod 'fame' and beraht 'bright'.
Samuel: Hebrew, 'name of God' or 'God has heard'. Biblical prophet.
Lowie: Flemish diminutive of Lodewijk (Louis), from Germanic 'famed warrior'.
Jack: English medieval pet form of John, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Léonie: French feminine of Léon, from Latin leo 'lion'.
Alma: Latin 'nourishing' or Spanish 'soul'; also Hebrew 'maiden' in some traditions.
Romée: Possibly a feminine form of Roméo, Italian 'pilgrim to Rome'. Dutch and Flemish use; origin uncertain.
Elisa: Short form of Elisabeth, from Hebrew 'God is my oath'.
Esmée: Old French esmé, 'esteemed' or 'loved', from Latin aestimare 'to value'.
Maryam: Arabic and Hebrew form of Mary, from Miriam. Mother of Jesus in the Quran.
James: English form of Jacob, from Hebrew Yaakov, possibly 'may God protect' or 'supplanter'.
Florence: From Latin Florentia, 'flourishing' or 'blooming'. The Italian city; Florence Nightingale popularised it.
Millie: English diminutive of Millicent or Amelia, Germanic 'strong in work'.
Alya: Arabic 'sublime' or 'exalted'; also Slavic and Hebrew uses. Possibly a variant of Aliyah.
Flo: Short form of Florence or Flora, from Latin 'flower'.
Julie: French form of Julia, a Roman clan name possibly meaning 'youthful'.
Ayla: Turkish 'moonlight' or 'halo'; also Hebrew 'oak tree'. Used across cultures.
Ilyas: Arabic and Turkish form of Elijah, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'.
Marius: Latin, a Roman clan name probably derived from Mars, the god of war.
Omar: Arabic, possibly 'long-lived' or 'flourishing'. Second caliph of Islam.
Mil: Probably a short form of names starting with Mil-, such as Milan or Emiel; origin uncertain.
Zayd: Arabic, 'growth' or 'abundance'. Adopted son of the Prophet Muhammad.
Haroun: Arabic form of Aaron; meaning uncertain, perhaps 'mountain of strength'. Made famous by Harun al-Rashid.
Hamza: Arabic, 'lion' or 'strong, steadfast'. Uncle of the Prophet Muhammad.
Lia: Italian and Spanish form of Leah, Hebrew 'weary' or 'wild cow'; also short for names ending in -lia.
Mats: Scandinavian and Dutch short form of Matthias, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Lyam: Variant spelling of Liam, Irish short form of William, Germanic 'resolute protector'.
Nolan: Irish, from Ó Nualláin, perhaps 'descendant of the champion' or 'noble'. Originally a surname.
Adèle: French form of Adela, from Germanic adal 'noble'.
Mattia: Italian form of Matthias, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Rosie: English diminutive of Rose, from the flower.
Amelia: Latinised Germanic amal 'work, industrious', blended with Latin Aemilia. Popular in English and Spanish.
Sarah: Hebrew, 'princess'. Wife of Abraham in the Bible.
Tuur: Flemish short form of Arthur, possibly from Celtic 'bear'.
Max: Short form of Maximilian or Maxim, from Latin maximus 'greatest'.
Valentina: Italian and Spanish feminine of Valentinus, from Latin valens 'strong' or 'healthy'.
Maya: Multiple origins: Sanskrit 'illusion', Hebrew 'water', Greek 'mother' or a month name, and a variant of Maria. Widely used.
June: English, from the month, named after the Roman goddess Juno. Used as a girls' name since the early 20th century.
Andrea: Italian boys' name from Greek andreios 'manly, brave'; used for girls in other countries.
Yasmine: French form of Jasmine, from Persian yasmin, the flower.
Julien: French form of Julian, from Latin Julianus, derived from the clan name Julius.
Margaux: French form of Margot, short for Marguerite, from Greek margarites 'pearl'.
Enzo: Italian short form of Lorenzo or Vincenzo; also used for Enrico. Meaning follows the full forms, 'laurel' or 'conquering'.
August: From Latin augustus, 'venerable' or 'majestic'. Title of Roman emperors.
Eliott: Variant spelling of Elliot, English surname from Elias, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'.
Stella: Latin, 'star'. Also an epithet of the Virgin Mary, Stella Maris.
Estelle: French form of Stella, from Latin 'star'.
Lola: Spanish pet form of Dolores, 'sorrows', referring to Our Lady of Sorrows.
Tom: English short form of Thomas, from Aramaic 'twin'.
Youssef: Arabic form of Joseph, from Hebrew 'God will add'. A prophet in Islam.
Charly: Variant spelling of Charlie, diminutive of Charles, from Germanic 'free man'.
Helena: Latin and Greek form of Helen, probably 'torch' or 'shining light'.
Vince: English short form of Vincent, from Latin vincens 'conquering'.
Miel: Flemish short form of Emiel, from Latin Aemilius; also French 'honey'.
Cézanne: French, from the surname of painter Paul Cézanne. Used as a modern given name; its etymology is unclear.
Morris: English form of Maurice, from Latin Maurus 'dark-skinned' or 'Moorish'.
Côme: French form of Cosmas, from Greek kosmos 'order, adornment'. Saint Cosmas.
Ezio: Italian, from Greek 'eagle' or 'beautiful'; possibly related to Aetius, a Roman general. Origin debated.
Daniel: Hebrew, 'God is my judge'. Biblical prophet.
Odette: French, from Germanic od 'wealth'. Famous as the Swan Queen in Swan Lake.
Amina: Arabic, 'trustworthy' or 'faithful'. Mother of the Prophet Muhammad.
Cyriel: Flemish form of Cyril, from Greek kyrios 'lord'.
Boris: Slavic, probably from 'fight' or 'small wolf', or from Turkic bogoris. Borne by saints and Bulgarian tsars.
Eléonore: French form of Eleanor, probably from Provençal Aliénor; origin debated, possibly 'the other Aenor'.
Dré: Short form of Andre or Andreas, from Greek andreios 'manly'. Also a Dutch nickname.
Maxine: Feminine form of Max or Maxime, from Latin maximus 'greatest'.
Aria: Italian 'air' or 'melody'; also Persian 'noble'. Modern popular name.
Warre: Flemish short form of Warner, Germanic 'protecting army', or from 'war'. Origin uncertain.
Jayden: Modern American coinage, blending Jay with the -den ending. Possibly linked to Hebrew Jadon 'thankful'.
Cilou: Modern name, probably a pet form of Cécile or Lou. Origin uncertain.
Mira: Slavic 'peace' or 'world', or Latin 'wonderful', or Sanskrit 'ocean'. Meaning varies by culture.
Loïc: Breton form of Louis, from Germanic 'famed warrior'.
Léna: French form of Lena, short form of Hélène or Madeleine.
Tiago: Portuguese form of James, from Hebrew Yaakov. Originally Santiago, 'Saint James'.
Lars: Scandinavian form of Laurence, from Latin Laurentius 'from Laurentum' or 'laurel'.
Lea: Form of Leah, Hebrew 'weary' or 'wild cow'.
Oona: Irish Úna, possibly 'lamb' or 'unity'; also Finnish and Latin variants. Origin uncertain.
Lukas: German and Dutch form of Luke, from Greek Loukas, 'man from Lucania' or 'light'.
Levi: Hebrew, 'joined' or 'attached'. Son of Jacob, ancestor of the Levites.
